title: Actual normal comparison of etale coordinate diagonals
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $n\geq1$ and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $Y$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme, let $h:U\to Y$ be smooth separated of finite type and pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, and let $e:U\to A=\mathbf A^d_Y$ be an etale $Y$-map, where $U$ is finite type over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Put $p:A\to Y$, so $h=pe$. Use fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] $W=U\times_YU$, $W_A=A\times_YA$, with first projections $p_U,p_A$ and diagonal closed immersions $\Delta_U,\Delta_A$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $Z=U\times_AU\subset W$ and $O=W\setminus(Z\setminus\Delta_U(U))$, with its induced open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. Write $i:O\hookrightarrow W$ and $q=(e\times e)|_O:O\to W_A$. Both diagonal immersions are regular of codimension $d$ and their normal bundles are the relative tangent bundles [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion, def-pur-normal-bundle]. Let $\mathcal G_U,\mathcal G_A$ be their conormal graded algebras [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], using $O$ for the first ambient scheme. The actual graded comparison of [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change] is an isomorphism
$$c:e^*\mathcal G_A\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G_U,$$
with affine formula $[a]\otimes r\mapsto[q^\sharp(a)r]$. Its degree-zero component is the identity and its degree-one component is the canonical conormal pullback map of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-flat-base-change]. Passing to relative spectra [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec] gives the specific isomorphism
$$N_{\Delta_U/W}=N_{\Delta_U/O}\xrightarrow{\sim}U\times_A N_{\Delta_A/W_A}.$$
It preserves projection and zero section, and under the tangent-bundle identifications it is the differential $de:T_{U/Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}e^*T_{A/Y}$. More precisely, the degree-one coordinate difference from the two factors of $W_A$ pulls back to the corresponding difference of its two pulled-back coordinates on $O$; this fixes the differential convention on both sides. Restricting $W$ to $O$ does not change its conormal graded algebra on the diagonal. These identifications include $d=0$ and the empty source.

proof.text: Construct the open O explicitly as the complement of the closed image of the complement of the etale diagonal in U times_A U. The map U times_A U to U times_Y U is a closed immersion, since p is separated. Its inverse image of O is precisely the etale diagonal. The open-immersion pullback criterion gives the Cartesian square, and the product of the two etale chart maps gives q etale. For positive d use the stated regular-diagonal theorem. For d=0, h and p are etale, their diagonal stalk maps are isomorphisms, and the empty sequence generates the zero kernel and preserves Krull dimension.

Apply the actual conormal graded flat base-change map to the chart square and to restriction to O, using the identity map on the centre for the latter. Both maps are invertible and retain every normalization in IsBaseChangeMap, including the canonical degree-one conormal map.

Construct the relative-spectrum map from the corresponding sheaf algebra map using global sections on the affine target and the affine-scheme adjunction. Prove its section formula on all opens by quasi-coherent module extensionality. For its Cartesian property, compare the module on the actual scheme pullback using affine pushforward base change and the module base-change algebra formula. The affine-scheme/quasi-coherent-algebra anti-equivalence reflects the resulting isomorphism. For the restriction over the identity base, use the same anti-equivalence directly.

Obtain the normalized diagonal derivation and prove its universal map from relative differentials invertible on the affine-open basis by the affine comparison theorem. Identify the ideal-sheaf model with the categorical kernel via the injective ideal inclusion. Transporting along this identification gives the required conormal isomorphism on arbitrary opens, with convention p2*a-p1*a.

The centred-coordinate theorem applied to the diagonal section of the first smooth projection proves that the canonical Sym(conormal) to conormal graded algebra map is invertible. Compose it with Sym of the normalized differential isomorphism and apply the relative-spectrum anti-equivalence. The counit fixes the section formula and the symmetric-algebra universal property identifies the augmentations, giving the required normal/tangent isomorphisms and zero-section identities. For the graded chart and restriction maps, degree-one extensionality shows that augmentation commutes: both composites vanish on degree one.

Represent the differential da by the ideal section p2*a-p1*a on the intersection of the two inverse images of its domain. The canonical degree-one base-change formula pulls this representative back by q; restriction to O pulls the corresponding representative on U times_Y U back by the open immersion. The two included ideal sections agree, by the two projection identities for q, so injectivity of the ideal inclusion identifies their conormal classes. Gradedness gives the same identity in the graded algebras. Conjugate the actual normal map by the constructed normal/tangent isomorphisms. Their section formulas and this identity show exactly da maps to d(e*a), proving IsDifferential. Transport the normal Cartesian square along these isomorphisms. All arguments preserve empty sources and d=0.

The statement is unchanged. Its 14 bracket citations are exactly the stmt_deps, and proof_deps is the union of the 16 step uses. There is no SGA citation. Step 1: lem-pur-chart-cartesian-domain is applied with X=U, j=id and V=Y (Y affine). All its hypotheses hold, and it gives O, the Cartesian square of centres and q étale, hence flat. lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion needs neither d>=1 nor properness. Step 2: lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change is applied with (g,i',f)=(q,Delta_A,e). It gives the actual c with [a]⊗r -> [q#(a)r], c_0=id, c_1 the conormal map, and c an isomorphism. This matches Stacks 0635 (divisors.tex line 4454) and 0473. Step 3: restricting to the open neighbourhood O is elementary and correct. Step 4: relative Spec, its anti-equivalence and its base change (Stacks 01LX) give the map, and since c is graded with c_0=1, epsilon_U c = e*epsilon_A, so the zero sections correspond. Step 5: with the convention p2*a-p1*a -> da (Stacks 08S2), q=e×e gives c_1(da)=d(e*a). Uniqueness of algebra maps out of Sym (lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core) then identifies the map with de. The direction was checked. The step implicitly uses Sym C ≅ G for a regular immersion as part of the Step 1 identification, which is acceptable. Step 6: the empty source and the d=0 case are correct. Small cases checked: identity, a coordinate permutation, t->t^m on G_m with m invertible (d(t^m)=m t^(m-1) dt), and the two-sheet étale cover in d=0. No duplicate among the DAG's chart, normal-bundle and differential nodes; the sibling lem-pur-chart-dnc-vector-factors consumes this map. The 9 generic tool_uses are accepted. This is a general scheme fact that neither the trace formula nor Poincaré duality gives, and it is not a step of either.
